context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_002-049_note.section: ## What these pages add to the supplied plan
context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_002-049_note.text: The most direct continuation is toward the reported formalism in **098–146**: flat resolutions and pullback in 100–106, coefficient and boundedness warnings in 108–112, projection/Künneth questions in 112–120, and intrinsic endomorphism traces and finite Tor questions in 126–146. The geometric counit and top-degree trace of **020–036** must first be distinguished from those endomorphism traces, then compared through the duality formalism. This is a structural comparison, not a dating argument, and it does not close the later finite-level-to-adic compatibility task. The supplied result-status disposition and the primary-source comparison table below make those limits explicit.

context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.text: The principal handwritten sequence concerns derived operations, projection and Künneth, traces over finite coefficient rings, Tor bounds and the beginning of a Lefschetz–Verdier construction. It supports the README's broad SGA 4/5 placement, while the **24 reused typescript pages** also contain operator theory, ramification, relative divisors, local algebra and an axiomatic étale-topos exposition. Those typed sources are not silently assigned to Grothendieck's authorship or treated as his own conjectures.

context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.section: ### N03. The explicit question about general topoi
context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.text: The marginal question “est-ce vrai dans le contexte des topos généraux ?” is attached to the paragraph asserting preservation of flat modules and the resulting tensor comparison, so its scope should remain local to that argument. For morphisms of ringed topoi, the modern derived-pullback construction preserves suitable K-flat resolutions and commutes with derived tensor (The Stacks Project Authors, n.d., [Tag 06YV](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06YV), Lemmas 21.18.1–4). This confirms a precise modern formulation of the question rather than establishing which axioms the undated draft intended by “topos généraux.”

context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.section: ### N38. The deleted boundedness condition has mathematical consequences
context/same_cote_33/MPL_33_098-146_note.text: In the inserted phrase “loc. libre de t.f., et borné,” the words “et borné” are themselves deleted, so they cannot be treated as a surviving hypothesis on this page. An infinite direct sum of contractible two-term free complexes placed in disjoint, successively negative degrees represents the zero, hence perfect, derived object, yet its identity has no finite degreewise alternating sum on that unbounded representative. Thus the literal representative-based formula needs local bounded representatives or another specified interpretation; this is a conditional scope objection, not a reason to restore the deletion or deny the intrinsic trace of the perfect object.
